dedupe_keys.name: usgs pager earthquake impact alerts estimated fatalities and economic losses

description: PAGER (Prompt Assessment of Global Earthquakes for Response) is an automated USGS system that estimates the impact of significant earthquakes worldwide for emergency responders, aid agencies and the media. It compares the population exposed to each level of shaking intensity with country or region loss models based on past earthquakes, and issues colour-coded alerts from the estimated range of fatalities and economic losses: green for no response, yellow local or regional, orange national and red international. Each release also comments on the dominant vulnerable building types in the region, exposure and fatalities from past nearby earthquakes, and secondary hazards such as landslides, tsunami and liquefaction. Coverage: significant earthquakes worldwide, with results generally within 30 minutes and an archive searchable by event. Access: public web pages, the one-page onePAGER report and event data through the USGS earthquake site. Licence: U.S. government work. Caveats: shaking estimates are uncertain in the first hours and improve with more data, so users should use the newest release (see the disclaimer). Simulation uses: event-level loss benchmarks for validating building vulnerability and casualty models, and triggers for emergency response scenarios. Related records: the PAGER global building inventory.
